intro: On 27 October 2026, the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam was conducted in three shifts. Shifts 1 and 2 have been reported as overall Easy to Moderate, with varying difficulty across sections such as Quantitative Ability and Reasoning. The figures for good attempts are unofficial and should be treated as indicative only; SSC normalises scores across shifts for final ranking. Shift 3 is still pending, so no usable analysis is available for that shift yet.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty reported for the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam on 27 October 2026?
faqs.a: Both Shift 1 and Shift 2 were reported as Easy to Moderate overall, based on the majority of candidate feedback. Shift 3 has not been analysed yet, so its overall difficulty is currently unavailable.

faqs.q: How did candidates perceive the Quantitative Ability section on 27 October 2026?
faqs.a: In Shift 1, Quantitative Ability was described as the toughest part, featuring advanced calculations and a tight 15‑minute limit. In Shift 2, the difficulty varied widely, ranging from easy to difficult topics. No data is available for Shift 3 at this time.

faqs.q: What does the pending status of Shift 3 mean for the analysis of the 27 October 2026 exam?
faqs.a: Shift 3 is marked as pending, indicating that no usable analysis has been published yet. A review will be added once sufficient candidate evidence is collected.

faqs.q: Are the reported good‑attempts numbers for the 27 October 2026 exam reliable?
faqs.a: The good‑attempts ranges (e.g., 20–78 for Shift 1 and 65–88 overall for Shift 2) are unofficial figures provided by candidates and should be treated as indicative rather than definitive.

faqs.q: How does SSC normalise scores across the three shifts for the 27 October 2026 exam?
faqs.a: SSC applies a normalisation process that adjusts raw scores from each shift to a common scale, ensuring fair comparison among candidates regardless of the shift they attended.
